name: Archaeological Area of Agrigento
description: On a ridge above Sicily's southern coast, the Valley of the Temples preserves the Greek city of Akragas, founded in the 6th century B.C. Majestic Doric temples still stand along the skyline, while much of the ancient town lies buried beneath fields and orchards. At 1,300 hectares, it is Europe's largest archaeological park, and it also reveals Roman-era streets and early Christian burial areas.
